title: feature-flags-and-consumption-experiments-prd
author: Sofia Martinez
content:
Overview
========

Purpose: This PRD defines a cross-functional product for runtime feature-flagging and consumption-driven experimentation. The goal is to let product, platform, and sales teams create short-lived feature experiments (packaging, pricing, routing policies) that are gated by measurable consumption, quality, and SLO signals without developer deploys.

This document bundles: product overview, requirements, design constraints, rollout plan, pricing/packaging notes, acceptance criteria, and a release checklist.

Background and motivation
-------------------------
- Customers increasingly ask to trial value-aligned packaging (e.g., low-latency route + limited tokens) before committing to Dedicated or Private offers.
- Engineering wants fewer service deploys to run packaging experiments (reduce code churn, risk).
- Finance needs precise attribution of incremental consumption for experiments.

High-level goals (success metrics)
----------------------------------
1. Enable product teams to define and deploy feature flags that change routing, quotas, and package rules without code changes. Target: 90% of packaging experiments run through this system.
2. Provide reliable consumption attribution for A/B experiments with <= 2% measurement error for token counts.
3. Ensure experiments respect SLO & safety policies; no experiment may degrade 99th percentile latency by >10% cluster-wide.
4. Reduce time-to-launch for a packaging experiment from 2 weeks to <48 hours.

Key definitions
---------------
- Experiment: a named configuration that applies feature guards (routing, quotas, pricing multipliers) to a subset of customers or tokens.
- Gate: boolean or percentage rule that assigns a request to control/variant.
- Consumption attribution window: 24-hour rolling window used to compute billing/telemetry for experiments.

Requirements (functional)
-------------------------
1) Experiment authoring UI and API
   - Allow product managers to create experiments via Redwood Console and the Admin API.
   - Required fields: name, owner, duration (start/end), target selection (tenant IDs, segments, percentage), variant definitions (routing policy, quota overrides, price modifier).
   - Support templated variants (e.g., "low-latency-route + 50k token cap + price x0.9").

2) Runtime enforcement and signal collection
   - Flag evaluation service must resolve decision in <2ms added latency.
   - Routing decisions applied atomically for a request: model selection, region, and capacity tier.
   - Emit event logs for every evaluated request: experiment_id, variant_id, decision, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, trace_id.

3) Billing and attribution
   - Experiment-level billing buckets must map tokens to experiments and variants for reporting and invoicing.
   - Attribution accuracy SLA: mismatches <2% compared to raw runtime counters after daily reconciliation.

4) Safety and SLO enforcement
   - Experiments must declare failover and rollback policies.
   - System enforces a global safety constraint: experiments together may not cause any SLO breach beyond defined error budgets.

5) Observability and analysis
   - Automatic dashboards per experiment: traffic split, latency histograms, token cost delta, quality regressions (as defined by attached eval prompt set).
   - Exportable CSV/JSON for finance reconciliation.

Non-functional requirements
---------------------------
- Availability: flag evaluation must be available with 99.99% uptime.
- Performance: median decision latency <1ms; p99 decision latency <10ms.
- Consistency: decisions for same trace must be idempotent and sticky for a configurable session window (default 30 minutes).
- Security: only RBAC-approved users may create experiments; changes must be auditable.

Design constraints and considerations
-----------------------------------
- Minimize coupling to serving runtime: evaluation service should be a thin, highly cached layer with near-real-time sync to the config store.
- Backpressure: if evaluation service is unavailable, requests must default to safe control variants and be logged for reconciliation.
- Cost: tagging every request for experiments increases telemetry volume; sampling strategies must be configurable per-experiment.

Architecture sketch (textual)
----------------------------
1. Experiment Config Store (Postgres + changefeed) — stores experiment manifests and policy versions.
2. Flag Evaluation Cache — distributed low-latency cache deployed alongside edge routing planes.
3. Runtime Hooks — serving runtime calls evaluator at request admission; evaluator returns variant assignment and any quota overrides.
4. Attribution Pipeline — streaming events (Kafka) -> enrichment -> daily reconciliation job -> billing buckets.

Configuration table (example)
----------------------------
| Field               | Type    | Example                         | Comments                         |
|---------------------|---------|---------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| name                | string  | new-pricing-trial-mar-27        | human readable                   |
| owner               | string  | pm:sofia-martinez               | contact                          |
| start_time          | datetime| 2027-03-01T00:00Z               | ISO8601                          |
| end_time            | datetime| 2027-03-15T00:00Z               | optional                         |
| target_percent      | int     | 20                              | percent of matched traffic       |
| routing_policy      | string  | low-latency-route               | maps to runtime routing profiles |
| quota_override      | string  | "tokens_per_day:50000"        | json blob                        |
| billing_bucket      | string  | exp-2027-q1-packaging           | ties to finance buckets          |

Acceptance criteria
-------------------
- A console UI exists where a PM can create an experiment and launch to 10% of production traffic in <30 minutes.
- The runtime assigns variants consistently for a session window and emits the required event fields for 99.9% of requests.
- Billing reports link experiment usage to finance-ready CSVs with <2% daily reconciliation variance.
- Safety guardrails trigger an automatic rollback if p99 latency for any affected route increases by >10% for 5 consecutive minutes.

Rollout plan (phases)
---------------------
1) Alpha (internal only, engineering + finance) — 2 weeks
   - Minimal UI, API-only experiment creation, end-to-end attribution verification on canary tenants.
2) Beta (select customers) — 6 weeks
   - Full console UI, SLO guardrails enabled, early billing integration.
3) GA (public) — 4–8 weeks after Beta
   - Documentation, self-serve templates, pricing guidance for trials.

Pricing and packaging notes
--------------------------
- Experiments are free to run for internal and trial customers, but usage is tracked. Finance may bill "experiment consumption" as a separate reconciliation line for customers who convert to paid offers.
- We propose a standardized trial package: 50k tokens/day + low-latency routing for 14 days. Product can create variants that apply a price multiplier (e.g., 0.9) to measure willingness to pay.

Security, compliance, and audit
------------------------------
- All experiment changes must be logged to the audit log with who/what/when.
- Confidential customer segments must be marked restricted and require legal review prior to inclusion in any experiment.

Open questions / decisions needed
--------------------------------
- How long should sticky assignment persist for interactive vs batch workloads? (30m default proposed).
- Is per-token billing attribution sufficient for complex embeddings/semantic-search workflows where downstream costs vary?
- Should finance be allowed to auto-bill experiment consumption or only recommend invoice adjustments?

---------

     "name": "trial-low-latency-50k",
     "owner": "pm:sofia-martinez",
     "start_time": "2027-03-01T00:00Z",
     "end_time": "2027-03-15T00:00Z",
     "target_percent": 20,
     "variants": [
       {"id":"control","routing":"standard","billing_bucket":"baseline"},
       {"id":"variant-a","routing":"low-latency-route","quota_override":{"tokens_per_day":50000},"price_multiplier":0.9}
     ]
   }

2. Release checklist (minimum)
   - [ ] Config store schema migration applied to staging and prod
   - [ ] Flag evaluation cache deployed to edge planes
   - [ ] Console UI implemented and RBAC gated
   - [ ] Attribution daily job verified for accuracy on alpha tenants
   - [ ] Finance runbook written and reviewed
